children.title: A project's own code generators
children.text:
A project's own guidelines may add generators that write code from the nodes, alongside those of the SpecSheriff tools. A rule of the project's own guidelines refining this one lists these generators, with what each writes and from which nodes.

Each such generator always writes the same code from the same nodes. Its code is generated from the approved wordings of its nodes, as §s-qyjw8xez6t6adc3 says. While the rule that lists the generator is a draft, the code the generator has written stays as it is.
children.reason: A project may need generated code that the SpecSheriff tools do not write, such as code in another language, or code generated from nodes of the project's own kinds. This rule holds such code to the same conditions as the code those tools generate: it can be checked against its nodes, and it stays bound to approved nodes (§s-utvqbypzhmgndug).
examples: A project whose system is written in Go lists, in its own guidelines, a generator that writes Go types from the nodes describing its data formats.

decisions.problem: Code a project generates from its own kinds and fields, as runtime checks, enumerations or a registry its runtime reads, had no generator of SpecSheriff to write it and nothing holding it to its nodes.
decisions.ruling: The owner: a project's own generators are listed in one rule of its own guidelines with what each writes from which nodes; what one writes is held as the generated types are, waiting for that rule as for its nodes, and the generator writes the same from the same nodes.

decisions.ruling: The owner: the generator writes its code from the approved wordings of its nodes. While the rule that lists the generator is a draft, the code the generator has already written stays as it is.

children.title: What a SpecTag names
children.text:
A SpecTag in the system's code (§s-hheus6f395ynqvc) or in its tests names a rule that the code implements or that the test is written from.

Outside the system's code, such as in the repository's own tools and their tests, a SpecTag names only a rule of the guidelines. A project's own checks (§s-2fau85dfyyeq66m) and generators (§s-km4x4s26kv7pjze) are among those tools. Such a SpecTag never counts as implementing a rule of the base specification or of the technical appendix.
children.reason:
A SpecTag binds a rule to the code that implements it and to the tests written from it (§s-8xw4mgvpexyvw5q). The repository's own tools, including a project's own checks and generators, are not the system's code (§s-hheus6f395ynqvc).

The repository's own tools can be written from the rules of the guidelines in the same order as the system's code, with the test first, so a SpecTag binds them to those rules too. Counted toward a rule of the base specification or of the technical appendix, such a SpecTag would let a tool stand in for the system's code.
examples: A project's own check refuses a commit that contains a secret. Its test has the SpecTag of the rule of the project's own guidelines that the check carries out.

decisions.problem: Nothing held a project's own check or generator to the rule listing it: its code carries no tag, what a generator writes owes no test and is withheld from the reviewer.
decisions.ruling: The owner: the tests of a project's own checks and generators carry the sid of the rule listing them and are written first, as the SpecSheriff tools' own tests do by the owner's choice of 2026-10-28.

decisions.ruling: A technical replacement in line with the owner's rulings of the same day on a test's SpecTag and on a draft: a test names its node by its SpecTag, and the check that binds symbols to their nodes reads only the symbols of code other than tests.

children.title: The order in which tools and checks run on a commit and on a push
children.reason:
A project may run tools of its own on a commit or a push, such as a scan that checks that nothing internal reaches a public repository. Adopting SpecSheriff must not stop them, even where the SpecSheriff tools cannot run, for example on a machine without the SpecSheriff plugin. A team that needs the checks that the git hooks run to apply to everyone runs them in CI.

The order lets every check rely on what it reads: files in their final form and, where it reads nodes, nodes whose structure has passed the structure checks.
examples: A project's own guidelines list a formatter. On a commit, the formatter rewrites the files in the commit first, and the generators of the SpecSheriff tools then write their files. A scan for secrets, one of the project's own tools for the pre-commit hook, runs next. The checks that each key is written only once in each object and that each file complies with its JSON Schema follow, and the other checks of the SpecSheriff guidelines run last, on the final files.

decisions.problem: Taking up the method set where git looks for hooks, so a project's own tools run at a commit or a push, such as a scan that nothing internal reaches a public repository, had no place to run.
decisions.ruling: The owner: at a commit and at a push the SpecSheriff tools run their checks first, then the project's own tools, whatever the checks find; both must pass. Operations of git keep their names — commit, push, merge, merge request — and the text names the SpecSheriff tools as such.

decisions.ruling: The owner: they run in three steps, from the particular to the general: the tools that rewrite files, then the project's own checks and its other tools, then the checks of the SpecSheriff guidelines. After the first step, nothing changes what the commit contains.

decisions.ruling: The owner: they run in the first step, together with the generators of the SpecSheriff tools.

children.title: A procedure that writes the specification is idempotent
children.text:
Every procedure that writes the specification, or what is generated from it, is idempotent: run again on what its previous run left, it gives the same result and changes nothing.

Whoever writes a procedure needed only once, such as one that brings existing documents into the nodes, removes it once it has run.
children.reason: Whoever works on the specification may run such a procedure at any time, by hand or as part of a check, without knowing whether it has run before. One whose second run changed anything would damage the specification the next time it ran. A procedure needed only once is idempotent only on the state of the specification it was written for, so on a later state it can do damage.

decisions.ruling: The owner: it is stated of every procedure that writes the specification, by its standard name, idempotent.

decisions.ruling: The owner accepted a wording that keeps the paragraph. Whoever writes such a procedure carries the rule out, as with other rules that no check enforces.

children.title: Setting a repository up and taking SpecSheriff out of it
children.text: One procedure of the SpecSheriff tools sets a repository up for those tools, and another takes SpecSheriff out of it. Taking SpecSheriff out removes what setting the repository up wrote outside the specification. It also removes the settings of the SpecSheriff tools that the repository's configuration holds, including the entries that set the specification's approval status (§s-qzthyh7yqvfhsa2), its `strict` flag (§s-q3pfzyaxvpr2zj2) and the extensions that the project has chosen (§s-9ttvcwpqkehm58g). It leaves the specification, the bindings file (§s-kgbzk2ph9e6jfb4), the system's code (§s-hheus6f395ynqvc), and the repository's own tools and their tests as they are.
children.reason: A project can take up SpecSheriff or stop using it without knowing which files and settings the SpecSheriff tools need, and keeps its specification, which states what its system does, either way.

children.title: What is generated from the nodes is regenerated and never edited
children.text:
The SpecSheriff tools regenerate everything that is generated from the nodes after every change to them. What is generated as part of the system's code is generated from the approved wordings of the nodes (§s-qyjw8xez6t6adc3).

Nobody edits by hand anything that is generated. Nobody copies anything from what is generated back into the specification.
children.reason: A copy that is edited, fed back into the nodes or left to lag behind them becomes a second version of the rules, and sooner or later the two diverge. Regenerated at every change, a copy stays a view of the single source of truth (§s-xqs2e24mx5253ye).
examples: A human-readable export, for example in Markdown, the map of the specification and the instructions an agent reads are regenerated after every change to the nodes.

decisions.problem: A changed data record node could not be committed before its confirmation, since its commit passed neither with the generated types left behind it nor with new ones naming an unchecked node, while a rule could; and regenerating code from an unchecked node implemented what its owner had not confirmed.
decisions.ruling: The owner: code generated from the nodes follows only checked nodes; while one it is generated from is unchecked, it stays as it was and its lag is reported, not refused.

decisions.ruling: In line with the owner's ruling on §s-km4x4s26kv7pjze: what a project's own generators write into the system's code also waits for its nodes.

children.title: Code generated from approved wordings
children.text:
Whatever the SpecSheriff tools and a project's own generators (§s-km4x4s26kv7pjze) generate as part of the system's code (§s-hheus6f395ynqvc), they generate from the nodes' approved wordings (§s-5ah25f6gy99panq). The part generated from each node follows the last wording of that node that was approved, even if that approval has since been withdrawn. Nothing is generated from a node that has never been approved.

Where the approved wording of a node relies on a node that has never been approved, nothing is generated from the dependent node either, and the SpecSheriff tools report the dependent node by its sid.
children.reason:
A generated file often comes from many nodes, some of them drafts. The rule lets that file be regenerated as soon as each approval is given, yet implement only what the nodes' owners have approved (§s-utvqbypzhmgndug).

The code of a node whose approval has been withdrawn stays as it was, as the code of any rule that has become a draft does. Code generated from a node that relies on a node that has never been approved would implement the latter as well.
examples: The types of two data formats are generated into one file. An owner approves a change to the first format while the second is a draft under discussion. The types of the first format are regenerated from its new wording immediately, and the types of the second stay as its last approved wording describes them.

decisions.problem: It was unsettled whether the generation of code from the nodes belongs to the SpecSheriff guidelines or to an extension of them.
decisions.ruling: The owner: the generation of code stays in the SpecSheriff guidelines. The node moves out of the extension and comes right after the node on what is generated from the nodes.

decisions.problem: Generated code was regenerated only after every node it comes from had been approved, so a single draft held back a whole file of types.
decisions.ruling: The owner: the code is generated from the last approved wording of each node. Nothing is generated from a node that has never been approved.

decisions.problem: The node did not say what is generated from a node whose approval has been withdrawn, or from an approved node that relies on a node that was never approved.
decisions.ruling: The owner: the part generated from a node follows its last approved wording, even after that approval is withdrawn. Nothing is generated from a node whose approved wording relies on a node that was never approved, and the SpecSheriff tools report that node by its sid.

children.title: Revising a rule starts with its reason
children.text: Whoever revises a rule first checks why it exists. Where there is no longer a reason for it, they remove the rule rather than reword it.
children.reason: Reworded, a rule with no reason left would keep a requirement nobody needs.
